summary: One TLS handshake presents one server certificate. The unverified S2 attempt must end; enrollment is server-side and policy-driven, never during a pending connection; S6 is a new connection attempt whose channel turns green.

Each request is consumed at its destination CA and never reappears. The subordinate-CA request in the flashback carries a CA=true band and a must-read 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' tag, so it cannot read as the RDP request being forwarded to the root.
The root's self-signed seal is revealed as an existing property, not animated closed; the root performs no operation in the present.
The handshake proof has its own shape (a signature impression), distinct from every key and included in the C-11 silhouette checks.
The trust-store recall does not travel (transport none, era recall); it is a shimmer on the card already in the cradle.
B-04.1's text says the capsule pauses at the server's outbound port, framed with the AD node; it never goes to AD.
The model and the notes agree on the self-signed certificate's contents (subject CN; no SAN modelled).
The notes state that the template definition is read from the AD enrollment policy before key generation; B-04.1 is the CA-selection lookup.
hard_test: none (documentation-only; not expressible as a model test)
